summary: Fire TV OS cannot be installed on a VM: Amazon does not distribute Fire OS or Vega OS system images for emulators or virtual machines, and the Vega Virtual Device lacks Alexa voice services, so voice testing on virtualised targets is impossible by design (docs/quitasol/q0-capability-audit.md). Alexa speech recognition itself is only testable on Amazon hardware. The substitute evidence path: compile the Q3 MediaSession glue (contract QUITASOL-MEDIASESSION-RT/1-draft) into a real signed APK and exercise MediaSession transport dispatch (play/pause/fast-forward via `cmd media_session dispatch`) on a generic AOSP android-34 emulator, with the verdict taken from observed logcat only. An AOSP emulator is not Fire OS: nothing here claims Fire OS behaviour.

toolchain_setup.result: JDK 17, Android cmdline-tools, platform android-34, build-tools 34.0.0, platform-tools, emulator, system-images;android-34;google_apis;x86_64, kotlinc 2.0.21, androidx media 1.7.0 / core 1.13.1 from Google Maven.

kotlin_compilation.result: kotlinc 2.0.21 compiled the emitted glue with zero errors and zero warnings against android-34 + androidx.media. First real compile of the glue — supersedes the BLOCKED kotlin_compilation gate in quitasol-q3.json.

apk_build_and_sign.result: APK built (491863 bytes); d8 emitted a single classes.dex with no missing-class warnings; apksigner verify OK.

runtime_dispatch_aosp.environment: headless AOSP android-34 google_apis x86_64 emulator, AVD quitasol-test, KVM, boot ~340s

dispatches.play: routed to our onPlay override; intent_dispatched:playback
dispatches.pause: routed to our onPause override; intent_dispatched:playback
dispatches.fast-forward: no log line — correctly absent: no binding exists for this scene (unresolved intents bind nothing); absence observed, not assumed

findings: MediaSessionCompat without a PlaybackState is not the media button session on API 34: dumpsys showed 'Media button session is null' and dispatch routed nowhere (0 callbacks) until setPlaybackState(STATE_PLAYING, actions PLAY|PAUSE|FAST_FORWARD) was added. This is a real integration requirement, now baked into the dump_glue harness.
targetSdk-0 APKs are refused at install (INSTALL_FAILED_DEPRECATED_SDK_VERSION): packaging must set min/target SDK (aapt2 link --min-sdk-version/--target-sdk-version or uses-sdk in the manifest).
A manifest without a launcher activity leaves the process unstartable on a clean install (nothing to monkey/am start).
kotlin-stdlib must be dexed into the APK: NoClassDefFoundError kotlin/jvm/internal/Intrinsics at Application.onCreate otherwise.

androidx.versionedparcelable must be present: SystemUI MediaController attach crashes the process via MediaSessionCompat's GET_EXTRA_BINDER path. Real builds fetch androidx.versionedparcelable:versionedparcelable; the test host's proxy blocked Google Maven so minimal stub classes were used in the rebuild only. The repo harness notes this requirement.
The first build agent's APK failed install for reasons 1-3 above; the runtime verdict comes from the emulator agent's rebuild with those fixed plus the PlaybackState patch (disclosed in full).
runtime_dispatch_aosp.scope: Verdict covers the callback-to-intent dispatch table on stock Android. Alexa's speech recognition (the layer that would issue these dispatches from voice) is not present on AOSP and remains a hardware gate.

alexa_speech_verification.reason: Alexa speech recognition and voice-command routing are only testable on Amazon hardware; no VM substitute exists (Q0 audit: Vega Virtual Device lacks Alexa voice services, Fire OS images are not distributed).

fire_os_conformance.reason: The AOSP emulator is not Fire OS. Amazon's Media Session permission com.amazon.permission.media.session.voicecommandcontrol is unknown to stock Android; on the emulator it was exercised only as a declared-but-unenforced manifest permission. No Fire OS behaviour is claimed.

unchanged: The Quitasol proposal remains proposed, not ratified.
The lowering tier remains unresolved across manifest, plan and glue.
The glue has never been claimed to run on Fire OS; this VM test is explicitly an AOSP substitute.
crates are unchanged: the harness consumes the emitted glue, it does not modify quitasol-semantic.
next_unblock: Real-hardware verification: a Fire TV device to (a) confirm the Fire OS 14+ permission exemption observed in the Q0 audit and (b) run Alexa speech-to-dispatch end to end. The emulator harness (scripts/quitasol-vmtest.sh --with-emulator) is reproducible and now bakes in all five build/run findings.
